The modern editor’s translation corrected against Whitelock, p. 482: “If anyone traffics with a church, he is to pay compensation with lahslit.” → “If anyone traffics with a church, he is to pay compensation with lahslit. (expanded letters in italics: lahslit)”.

div.head: Northu 20
div.ab: Gif man mid cirican mangie, bete be lahslite.
Gif man mid cirican mangie, bete be lahslite.
Wenn jemand mit einer Kirche Handel treibt, büsse er durch Rechtsbruchbusse.
If anyone traffics in a church, let him atone with the fine for breach of law (lahslit).
If anyone traffics with a church, he is to pay compensation with lahslit.
If anyone uses a church as currency, he is to compensate for that with lahslit.
div.note: Liebermann compares VI Atr 15.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘If anyone traffics with a church, he is to pay with lahslit.’).; W: corrected against Rabin p. 307, October 2026 (was “If anyone uses a church as currency, he is to compensate for that with lahslit.”, now “If anyone uses a church as currency, he is to compensate for that with lahslit. (expanded letters in italics: lahslit)”)

note.seg: Auch hier ist das blosse Verbot in der Quelle in einen Fall mit zugefügtem Strafgeldfixum verwandelt, wie in 5—18. Die Quelle könnte an sich auch V Atr 10, 2 sein, doch geht dort nicht cyricgrið voran
Here too the mere prohibition in the source has been turned into a case with a fixed fine added, as in 5—18. The source could in itself also be V Atr 10, 2, but there cyricgrið does not precede
